Sahil @ Dharmendra
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Palash Choudhary - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Viraj Godha - G.A. for the State.
 Order
1.
They are heard.
Perused the case diary/challan papers.

2. This is the second application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 / 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.238/2024 registered at Police Station Pardesipura, District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Section 376, 376(2)(n), 450,
506 of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 30/05/2024.
3. His first bail application M.Cr.C. No.673/2025 was dismissed by this Court on 28/02/2025 with liberty to renew prayer after the prosecutrix is examined in the trial Court.

4. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the prosecutrix and her parents are deliberately not appearing in the trial Court since last 12 occasions and bailable warrants have also been issued but the prosecution has not been able to procure the presence of the witnesses, whereas the applicant is lodged in jail since 30/05/2024.

Counsel has submitted that otherwise also, the prosecutrix was a consenting party as admittedly the prosecutrix has also stated that she used to talk NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5970 2 MCRC-6066-2026 to the applicant since last around 4 years and because of her parents' objection, she stopped talking to the applicant

, hence, it is submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case, thus, deserves to be released on Sahil @ Dharmendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130512802/
1 bail.

entities.text: Sahil @ Dharmendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out, however, it is not denied that there is no DNA report available and the MLC is also negative.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the deposition of the prosecutrix, this Court finds force in the submissions as advanced by counsel for the applicant,
and further taking note of the fact that the applicant is lodged in jail since 30/05/2024 and final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court,
the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules

. 
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE krjoshi Sahil @ Dharmendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130512802/
